title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of a case-by-case classification, in 'Chirurgie des surfaces conformes', of when a compact conformal surface X (possibly non-orientable) carries a canonical Riemannian metric compatible with its conformal structure. The previous page treats the torus case (flat metrics), the real projective plane, and begins the case X ≅ P^1_C. This page handles the Riemann sphere, where Aut_conf(X) = G (PSL(2,C), extended by the anti-holomorphic maps) is non-compact, so there is no canonical metric, even up to a constant.

The remedy is to add extra structure: a closed subgroup H ⊂ G. For H to preserve a metric compatible with the conformal structure, H must be compact; Grothendieck notes this as a necessary condition. Let H^+ = H ∩ Aut^+(X), the orientation-preserving part.

Write X = P(V) with V a complex vector space of dimension 2. Let H̃ be the inverse image of H^+ in SL(V). It is a compact group (a double cover of H^+). By averaging (Weyl's unitarian trick) it preserves a positive definite hermitian form on V. Such a form gives a round (Fubini–Study) spherical metric on X, which can be normalized to total area 1.

When the invariant hermitian form is unique up to a positive scalar, H^+ alone determines a canonical normalized spherical metric on X. This happens exactly when V is an irreducible H̃-representation, by Schur's lemma together with complete reducibility.

This metric is invariant under Norm_G(H^+):
- an element normalizing H^+ carries the invariant ray of forms to itself;
- the area normalization then removes the scalar.
In particular the metric is invariant under H itself, since H normalizes its index ≤ 2 subgroup H^+, and this invariance characterizes it.

The next page treats the reducible case. There H^+ fixes two points z, z' and lies in the circle group T ≅ U(1) of the torus C* fixing them. The invariant metrics are then parametrized by the T-orbits on X \ {z, z'}, i.e. by the 'equator' circle.

In modern terms, this is the elementary fact that a compact subgroup of PSL(2,C) fixes a point of hyperbolic 3-space H^3, and that this fixed point is unique iff the subgroup does not fix a point of the boundary sphere. Here H^3 is viewed as the space of normalized round metrics on P^1 (equivalently, hermitian forms up to scalar).
errors: Minor: compactness is called a 'necessary' condition. For a closed subgroup it is in fact also sufficient, as the averaging argument on the same page shows. This is not an error, just understated.

Implicit: when H^+ is trivial (H̃ = {±1}), every form is invariant. Grothendieck handles this separately on the next page ('Si H^+ ≠ {1}'). The 'à vérifier' there concerns the claim that H^+-invariant metrics coincide with T-invariant ones; this holds when H^+ ≠ {1}.

ideas.what: Canonical metric on the Riemann sphere given by a compact subgroup H of conformal automorphisms with irreducible action, invariant under the normalizer
ideas.modern_name: Unitarian trick / Schur's lemma; fixed point of a compact group acting on H^3 = PSL(2,C)/SU(2) (Cartan fixed point theorem)

ideas.what: Case-by-case classification of canonical (normalized) metrics compatible with a conformal structure on compact surfaces, including non-orientable ones via the orientation double cover and descent of antipodally invariant metrics
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization / constant-curvature metrics in the conformal class
ideas.where_published: Related themes appear in Esquisse d'un programme (canonical metrics on surfaces linked to dessins and cartography), but not this computation

deep.surprise_reason: Standard representation-theoretic argument about compact subgroups of PSL(2,C) and invariant round metrics; it is a routine step in Grothendieck's systematic treatment of canonical metrics on conformal surfaces, with nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'invarie une métrique riemannienne[?] sphérique compat.' — the image reads more like 'invarie une métrique sphérique compat. avec la str. conforme' (no 'riemannienne').
Last line likely 'et ceci nous caractérise cette métrique' / 'et ces conditions la caractérisent' rather than 'caractérise cette condition'; the handwriting is uncertain.
'SL(V)' was written over an erased/corrected symbol; the reading SL(V) is correct.
